title: Associations of dietary diversity trajectories with cognitive impairment among Chinese older adults: A longitudinal cohort study
content:
by Zheng Shao, Zhiying Chen, Shiyi Xu, Jiayuan Jiang, Lina Gao, Kan Tian

Objective

To examine the trajectories of dietary diversity and their associations with cognitive impairment among older Chinese adults.

Methods

This study used longitudinal data from the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey (CLHLS) collected between 2008 and 2018, including 2455 participants. Group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) was applied to identify long-term patterns of dietary diversity. Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to estimate the associations between different dietary diversity trajectories and the risk of cognitive impairment.

Results

GBTM identified three latent trajectory groups characterized by different longitudinal patterns of the CLHLS-derived DDS: a “Low-Stable” group (n = 1033, 42.1%), a “Moderate-Stable” group (n = 1206, 49.1%), and a “High-Stable” group (n = 216, 8.8%). Compared with the Low-Stable group, the risk of cognitive impairment was 21% lower in the Moderate-Stable group (HR = 0.79, 95% CI:0.68–0.91) and 46% lower in the High-Stable group (HR = 0.54, 95% CI:0.39–0.75). Sensitivity analyses yielded results consistent with the main findings.

Conclusions

Distinct longitudinal patterns of the CLHLS-derived DDS were identified among Chinese older adults. Relatively higher dietary diversity trajectories were associated with a lower risk of cognitive impairment, suggesting that longitudinal dietary variety may be relevant to cognitive health in later life.
author: Zheng Shao
